# Final Year Project Journal

## Group \- AI4DB

# Group Work Journal Entries

## Week of November 10

* Completed the initial project proposal, which outlined the exploration of main database optimization topics.  
* Conducted initial research into three distinct aspects of database optimizations. A temporal graph of this early research is available [here](https://www.mermaidchart.com/d/0985d848-2aec-4220-ad0f-c94da23a33a6).

## Week of November 17

* Following feedback, we were asked to reduce the overall scope of the project.  
* Formulated a new plan to focus entirely on the topic of Knob-Tuning moving forward.

## Week of November 24

* Conducted key research on Knob-Tuning, focusing on the E2ETune paper: [\[2404.11581\] E2ETune: End-to-End Knob Tuning via Fine-tuned Generative Language Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11581).  
* Began exploring a key project objective: achieving E2ETune's reported performance improvement (around 51%) using a much lighter model (e.g., Deepseek R1 \- 1.5B) suitable for CPU-only inference, thereby avoiding the need for GPU resources![][image1]

## Week of December 1

* Set up necessary Virtual Machines (VMs) on Digital Ocean.  
* Cloned the E2ETune repository to begin local verification.  
* Fixed initial code issues in the repository, and successfully installed and configured the VM with Postgres and the IMDB database.

## Week of December 8

* Initiated the process of running workloads, starting with the SMAC optimizer.  
* Identified a discrepancy with the original paper's methodology (which used HEBO) and switched the codebase to utilize the HEBO python library for optimization.

## Week of December 15

* Started running the OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) workloads as part of the performance testing.

## Week of December 22

* Installed Benchbase, a tool necessary to begin running the OLTP (Online Transaction Processing) workloads.

## Week of December 29

* Began running the OLTP workloads.  
* Successfully completed the TPCC and Smallbank workloads.

## Week of January 5

* Running other OLTP workloads as well  
* Started training a cost model to predict the performance for a given configuration with currently available data.

## Week of January 12

- Started experimenting with retrieving query plans for each workload.  
- Writing code to retrieve workload features as well

## Week of January 19

- The cost model is now trained and has a R2 score of around 0.82, which is trained with data of query plans, workload features and internal metrics.  
- Modified workload running script to use cost model for remaining workloads.
